review: The first CBA season immediately established Cody Stalp as the person everyone else would have to explain away. Rim Lickster went 11-2, led the league with 1,517.86 points, and produced the season's 168.02-point high score. A seven-game winning streak made the inaugural regular season feel less like an introduction and more like a hostile takeover.

Peter Ganz and Will Leafstedt both finished 10-3, which was excellent preparation for discovering that only one of them could reach the final. Peter handled that problem in Week 15, beating Will 119.48-116.78 after Will had survived the opening round. Tim Switzer also reached the semifinal, where Cody ended the discussion by 26.36 points.

The title game stayed on brand. Cody scored 145.38, Peter scored 110.42, and the first CBA trophy went to the team that had already spent thirteen weeks making the case. Elsewhere, Patrick Czechut supplied the 21.18-point low, ensuring the inaugural year included both a champion and a useful warning label.
2017.championship: Cody Stalp entered the final as the 11-2 top seed and left with a 34.96-point win over Peter Ganz. Rim Lickster's 145.38 was not a dramatic escape; it was one last reminder that the regular-season evidence had been admissible the whole time.

review: Kelbey Heider went 12-1 in 2018, which is the kind of record that makes everyone else start auditing the schedule. Long Dick of the Law scored 1,594.26 points and opened the season with a 171.18-point week. Will Leafstedt technically led the league in total points at 1,604.92, earning the important distinction of winning the spreadsheet without winning the trophy.

The bracket offered several opportunities for order to collapse. Cody Stalp beat Tim Switzer by 4.54 in the opening round, then put up 114.06 while Cody Leslie managed 65.66 in the semifinal. Kelbey removed Will with a 41.08-point semifinal win, ending the league's highest-scoring season before it reached the final.

The championship was less suspense than paperwork. Kelbey beat Cody Stalp 126.14-61.08, a 65.06-point margin, and collected his first title. A 12-1 regular season followed by two comfortable playoff wins is annoyingly difficult to describe as luck.
2018.championship: Kelbey Heider's first championship came with a 126.14-61.08 win over Cody Stalp. The 65.06-point margin remains the central fact; any attempt to build suspense around it would be historical vandalism.

review: Wes Dempsey owned the 2019 regular season. Great White Hope went 11-2, led the league with 1,497.24 points, and posted a 185.56-point high in Week 8. Peter Ganz finished one game back at 10-3, apparently content to let Wes collect every regular-season receipt before disputing the final invoice.

Austin Ketter and Tim Switzer escaped the opening round, but neither survived the semifinals. Wes edged Austin 120.66-118.72, while Peter scored 155.78 to move past Tim by 26.96. Cody Leslie contributed the season's closest finish, a 0.22-point win, proving that a 2-11 record can still contain one extremely specific triumph.

Peter saved the reversal for Week 16. Fresh out of AJ Greenz scored 149.92 against Wes's 137.78, turning the league's best regular-season team into the runner-up. Peter's first title came from a 12.14-point final that was close enough to hurt and clear enough to avoid litigation.
2019.championship: Peter Ganz beat Wes Dempsey 149.92-137.78 after Wes had led the regular season in both wins and points. Fresh out of AJ Greenz picked the final week to become the one statistic Wes could not top.

review: The 2020 table finished with Kelbey Heider and Alex Continenza both at 9-4. Will Leafstedt scored a league-best 1,449.54 points, while Jawad Najdawi assembled the longest winning streak at five games. The standings were balanced enough to suggest a competitive postseason, which the championship game would later treat as a funny misunderstanding.

Kelbey beat Ben Christianson 105.34-96.02 in one semifinal. Alex handled Peter Ganz 112.76-95.92 in the other, setting up a final between the top two regular-season records. Will's season also included a 0.08-point win, the fantasy equivalent of finding a coin under the couch and insisting it was strategic.

Then Kelbey scored 191.00 points in the championship. Alex scored 102.12, a normal football total that became scenery next to the highest eligible single-game score in CBA history. Kelbey's second title arrived by 88.88 points and permanently removed the phrase 'anything can happen in the final' from responsible analysis.
2020.championship: Kelbey Heider's 191.00-102.12 win over Alex Continenza was both a championship and a league-record scoring performance. Long Dick of the Law turned the final into the statistical equivalent of a venue evacuation.

review: Bradley Dillon finished 2021 at 10-4 and took the top regular-season record. Will Leafstedt, Peter Ganz, and Cody Leslie followed at 9-5, while Jack Haley led the entire league with 1,566.96 points and still finished 7-7. Jack won the Points Without Peace award before anyone had formally invented it.

Cody and Peter won the opening playoff games, only to meet the top seeds in Week 16. Bradley beat Cody 138.70-100.04. Will was even less diplomatic, scoring 153.56 against Peter's 77.30. Shawn Smith supplied the season's 0.02-point closest win, because apparently two hundredths is enough room for a victory lap.

The final belonged entirely to Will. Nut Kupp beat Henry's Heros 114.00-50.82, giving Will his first championship and Bradley a runner-up finish after leading the regular season. The 63.18-point margin left no meaningful alternate interpretation.
2021.championship: Will Leafstedt defeated Bradley Dillon 114.00-50.82 for his first CBA title. Bradley brought the best regular-season record; Will brought 63.18 more championship points.

review: Will Leafstedt led 2022 in both record and scoring, finishing 10-4 with 1,513.04 points. Cody Stalp and Bradley Dillon went 9-5, as did eventual champion Jawad Najdawi. The regular season therefore identified Will as the favorite and the postseason identified that information as nonbinding.

Jawad beat Cody Leslie by 6.86 in the opening round, then eliminated Will 113.66-82.88. Alex Continenza took the other route, beating Bradley Dillon and then Cody Stalp by 4.68. Will still collected the season's closest eligible win at 0.14 and biggest regular-season blowout at 92.32, two excellent facts that remained stubbornly non-trophies.

Joe Smith's Dab Express finished the job in Week 17. Jawad beat Alex 113.76-91.70 and became CBA champion after entering the bracket at 9-5. Three consecutive playoff wins made the path longer than most title runs and considerably more useful than a first-place regular-season seed.
2022.championship: Jawad Najdawi beat Alex Continenza 113.76-91.70 to win the 2022 championship. Joe Smith's Dab Express completed a three-win bracket run and left the regular-season favorite with several impressive non-championship statistics.

review: Peter Ganz went 10-4 and produced an eight-game winning streak, the cleanest regular-season résumé in 2023. Bradley Dillon somehow scored a league-high 1,555.32 points and finished 6-8, which is an efficient way to become both impressive and furious. Tim Switzer led the playoff-bound middle at 7-7 with 1,489.40 points.

Kelbey Heider entered at 8-6 and beat Shawn Smith, then top-seeded Peter. Tim eliminated Jason Nitz and Will Leafstedt, scoring 123.54 and 106.40 along the way. Jason's 0.04-point closest win and Bradley's 93.72-point regular-season blowout gave the year suitable extremes before the bracket narrowed to familiar names.

Kelbey beat Tim 102.78-95.00 in the final and claimed his third championship. It was not Kelbey's best regular season, which only made the ending more irritating for everyone who had spent fourteen weeks above him.
2023.championship: Kelbey Heider defeated Tim Switzer 102.78-95.00 for title number three. Long Dick of the Law entered the postseason at 8-6, then removed Shawn Smith, Peter Ganz, and Tim in order.

review: Cody Leslie produced the loudest regular season in CBA history: 13-1, 1,621.28 points, and a thirteen-game winning streak inside the season. Jason Nitz also cleared 1,600 points, while Wes Dempsey went 11-3. For fourteen weeks, Punani Dasani made the league look solved.

The bracket declined to cooperate. Tim Switzer beat Will Leafstedt by 0.36 in the opening round, then scored a season-high 167.54 to eliminate Cody by 45.36. Wes beat Jawad Najdawi by 1.68 in the other semifinal, a much less theatrical route to the same destination.

Wes won the final 126.82-102.28 over Tim and collected his first championship. Cody's 13 wins remain the regular-season headline, while The Kekambas kept the only line that ends with 'Champion.' Fantasy football remains committed to separating achievement from emotional closure.
2024.championship: Wes Dempsey defeated Tim Switzer 126.82-102.28 for the 2024 title. The Kekambas survived a 1.68-point semifinal and then won the championship by 24.54, completing the bracket run that the 13-1 favorite could not.

review: Kelbey Heider spent 2025 reminding everyone that four championships is no longer an accident. Long Dick of the Law finished 10-4, led the league with 1,642.64 points, and took the top regular-season spot. Alex Continenza, Wes Dempsey, and Jawad Najdawi all finished 9-5, close enough to make the bracket credible and not close enough to stop the familiar ending.

Jawad and Wes opened the playoffs with 168-point weeks. Kelbey answered by beating Jawad 157.88-98.92, while Wes moved past Alex 97.90-89.32. Jason Nitz supplied the regular season's longest winning streak at five games; Peter Ganz supplied the 7.60-point eligible low in Week 14, an unforgettable contribution for entirely different reasons.

The final was the season's actual argument. Kelbey beat Wes 116.76-114.50, a 2.26-point finish that gave him championship number four. Wes came closer than anyone had in Kelbey's previous title games, which is a meaningful historical achievement and an exceptionally poor substitute for the trophy.
2025.championship: Kelbey Heider defeated Wes Dempsey 116.76-114.50 in the closest CBA championship of Kelbey's four title runs. A 2.26-point margin separated another Wes runner-up finish from Kelbey making the dynasty label unavoidable.
